name: std float parsing (Eisel-Lemire, Rust 1.55)
baseline: std's float parsing before Rust 1.55 (dec2flt with Clinger's AlgorithmM and Bellerophon)
verdict_reason: Rust 1.55 (2021-09-09) replaced dec2flt with an Eisel-Lemire implementation adapted from fast-float. The PR put the old parser at 130 MiB/s on canada against up to 1200 MiB/s for the new algorithm, and published tables show from_str going from 7.3x-8.1x behind fast-float on Rust 1.49 to 1.19x-1.20x behind on Rust 1.81/1.83, and ahead on large integer-valued floats.
tier_reason: The fast-float tables come from a public benchmark tool with CPU, OS and Rust version stated; the throughput figures are from the rust-lang PR.
claimed_speedup: PR #86761: old std 130 MiB/s on canada vs up to 1200 MiB/s for Eisel-Lemire on Apple M1 (10x). canada from_str vs fast-float: 174.43 vs 21.58 ns (Rust 1.49, i7-4771) and 190.06 vs 25.90 ns (Rust 1.49, AMD Rome); 11.59 vs 9.77 ns (Rust 1.81, i7-14700K) and 22.90 vs 19.17 ns (Rust 1.83, EPYC 7763) (ratios derived from page data)
workload: Parsing f64 from text: canada.txt coordinates and synthetic datasets; ns per value or MiB/s.
hardware: Apple M1 (PR figure); Intel i7-4771 and AMD Rome (Rust 1.49 tables); Intel i7-14700K and AMD EPYC 7763 (current tables)
one_liner: Since Rust 1.55, str::parse::<f64> uses Eisel-Lemire and runs within about 1.2x of fast-float, down from 7x-8x behind.
how_it_is_fast: Eisel-Lemire handles inputs with up to 19 significant digits using 128-bit products against a power-of-five table, with a fast path for exactly representable values and a simple big-decimal fallback for long inputs. The PR also parses eight digits at a time with three multiplications.
use_it_when: Any f32/f64 parsing from &str: this is the default and needs no dependency
skip_it_when: You need partial parsing or parsing straight from &[u8]; use fast-float2 or lexical-core
caveats: Before/after ratios compare tables from different CPUs; each ratio is within one machine
The 1200 MiB/s figure is for the algorithm on Apple M1, not a measurement of the merged std code
tradeoffs: None for callers; the PR reports similar stripped code size and much smaller unstripped binaries

evidence.quote: The standard library's implementation of float parsing has been updated to use the Eisel-Lemire algorithm, which brings both speed improvements and improved correctness.
- [Updated std's float parsing to use the Eisel-Lemire algorithm.][86761]
speeds up to 1200 MiB/s on Apple's M1 architecture
- CPU: Intel i7-14700K 3.40GHz - OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL2) - Rust: 1.81
- CPU: AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor 3.20GHz - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.1 - Rust: 1.83
